static_traits.name: Lin Kai
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, without parents or siblings
static_traits.social_status: Has a few acquaintances to talk with, but finds it hard to maintain close relationships due to inadequacy, and hard to open up about self-doubt with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness history; no similar psychological issues or treatment/counseling experience in the past
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude, clear expression, willing to cooperatively explore and self-reflect

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I will never succeed in this life because I work at a grocery store, causing self-doubt and low self-worth; over time, especially when seeing others' career achievements, these feelings become more frequent and intense.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to resolve debilitating self-doubt and explore ways to improve self-worth.
growth_experiences: After several job-seeking failures a few years ago, entered work at a grocery store; at first viewed it as a temporary choice, but continuous rejection letters gradually made them believe 'this may be the only thing I can do'.
Repeatedly comparing when hearing of or seeing friends' promotions and new jobs, reinforcing pessimistic anticipation about the future and ability.
Each rejection is interpreted as 'I am not good enough/not smart enough', and such interpretations gradually consolidate negative self-beliefs.

core_beliefs: I am destined not to succeed
I am not good enough/not smart enough
My worth depends on having a decent job

special_situations.event: Sees friends posting news of promotions or new jobs on social media
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are more successful while I have no respectable job, it means I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids further disappointment by comparing with others and lowering expectations of herself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them, I am just a failure

special_situations.event: Received notice of a job application rejection
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am rejected, it proves I have no ability and will not succeed in the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces further applications or procrastinates job hunting to avoid further setbacks
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This proves again I am not good enough; I will never get out of this in my life

special_situations.event: Thinking while working at the grocery store that one's position is not 'respectable'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Job titles determine personal worth; having no respectable job equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using self-deprecation and the idea of 'not holding expectations' to protect oneself from disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: People like me will never succeed

special_situations.event: Last week saw a friend's social media update about a new position at a tech company
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am still in this job now, it means I will never get out
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Presetting the worst outcome in advance to lower the gap, no longer holding hope
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never get rid of this dead-end job

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and succeed, proving one's worth and ability
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected again and seen as incompetent, thus losing the sense of worth and connection
defense_goal: Avoids disappointment by lowering expectations and self-deprecation
Keeping some distance from others to avoid exposing inadequacy and frustration

object_relations.self_representation: A low-value 'incompetent person' prone to failure

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to explore the function or benefits of negative beliefs and consider letting go of these thoughts
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying that holding hope will lead to being rejected again, thus tending to find reasons to maintain low expectations
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone flat, emphasizing the 'protective effect' of maintaining low expectations, using expressions like 'if I do not hold expectations, I will not be too disappointed'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reviewing multiple job rejections or comparing with friends' success
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Separates painful emotions from experiences, talking more in a factual listing manner to avoid directly facing shame and sadness
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Stating experiences in objective, brief descriptions, avoiding emotional words and details, quickly turning to countermeasures or conclusions.

manifestations: Views 'decent job = success' as the sole or main source of meaning
While working at the grocery store, feels 'this is a dead end'
Growing pessimism about the future and ability
Living alone without parents or siblings
Difficulty maintaining close relationships due to inadequacy
outcomes: Harder to ask for help in difficult situations

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizes 'only having a decent job counts as success' as an absolute standard

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently evaluating oneself with 'I am not good enough/not smart enough'
When discussing action plans, shows caution and self-limitation with 'sounds a bit scary'
Finding it hard to open up about self-doubt with acquaintances

exception_events.target_problem: When seeing others' career progress or receiving job rejection letters, the client usually falls into 'I will never succeed' thoughts, with low mood and reduced job-seeking actions.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In the past obtained several interview opportunities during job seeking, able to submit resumes on time and complete interview preparation, experiencing that possibilities are not entirely absent.
exception_events.reason: Clues: the practice of continuously submitting resumes and basic application preparation; learning that someone progressed after starting from an entry-level position provided a different reference.

positive_force: Still continuously submitting resumes, once obtained interview opportunities
Possessing reflective ability, able to identify the 'protective function' of negative thoughts
Willing to try goal setting and skill learning (e.g. weekly applications, online courses)
Can propose more balanced alternative statements; subjective sense of control somewhat improves
negative_force: Excessively compares with others, relies on external evaluation to define self-worth
Cognitive biases like black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization and predicting the future reinforce the sense of failure
Self-labeling and self-doubt, leading to decreased motivation and impaired self-care
After job setbacks, reduces action to avoid disappointment (behavioral avoidance)
Weak social support; hard to ask others for help

target_behavior.behavior: Recurring negative automatic thoughts like 'I will never succeed' and self-deprecation
antecedent: Seeing news of friends' promotions/new jobs
Received notice of a job application rejection
Thinking at work that the position is not 'respectable'
target_behavior.core_reason: Equating job respectability with personal worth, long-term comparison with others, and interpreting rejection letters as personal incompetence
target_behavior.function: Avoids disappointment and shame, gaining short-term psychological protection through self-limitation
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and decreased sense of self-worth, affected work performance and daily self-care

antecedent: Anticipating the emergence of 'I will not succeed' thoughts
target_behavior.core_reason: Helplessness caused by catastrophizing and overgeneralization, worrying about failing again and being negated
target_behavior.function: Escaping possible failure and negative evaluation, briefly lowering anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Fewer opportunities, staying in the current position, further reinforcing the belief of 'never succeeding'
